objective.statement: Know the additional instruments of Grade 5: relatives of the Grade 4 woodwinds, trombones, extra percussion, and non-orchestral instruments.
successCriteria: I know the piccolo, cor anglais, bass clarinet and double bassoon and the instrument each is related to.
I know definite and indefinite pitch percussion.
I know which instruments are not regular members of the orchestra.

explanation.text: Woodwind. The piccolo is a small flute, so it sounds higher. The cor anglais is similar to the oboe but deeper. The bass clarinet is a deeper clarinet. The double bassoon is a deeper bassoon. Except for the flute and the piccolo, all of these use reeds: one reed for the clarinets, two for the oboe family and the bassoons.

Brass. A full orchestra normally has two tenor trombones and one bass trombone (also called a tenor-bass trombone). The cello, the bassoon and the tenor trombone can read the tenor clef for their higher notes.

Percussion. Instruments of indefinite pitch (no particular notes) include the triangle, tambourine, castanets and tam-tam (gong). Instruments of definite pitch (they play notes) include the xylophone, marimba, glockenspiel, vibraphone, celesta and tubular bells. The timpani, which you know already, have definite pitch.

Some of the most widely used instruments are not regular members of the standard orchestra: the guitar, saxophone and recorder, for example. The piano is another: it often appears as a soloist with an orchestra. Other keyboard instruments are the harpsichord, the clavichord and the organ. Organ music is normally written on three staves: the lowest is for the pedal-board.
